prompt: Complete WordSearcher.countWord so it counts case-insensitive whole-word occurrences of a word across every line of a file (so "cats" and "scattered" never match "cat").
explanation: Splitting each line with the regex \W+ breaks it on any run of non-word characters (spaces, commas, punctuation), leaving only the actual words. Comparing tokens with equalsIgnoreCase gives a case-insensitive whole-word match, so substrings like "cat" inside "scattered" never count. A simple contains() check would get this wrong -- tokenizing first is what makes the match whole-word.
hints: Files.readAllLines(p) gives you every line; loop over them.
line.split("\\W+") splits a line into words, discarding punctuation between them.
Compare each token to the target with equalsIgnoreCase and increment a counter on match.
